facts.statement: The type locality of Eopavo is the Liushu Formation.
Eopavo fossils were found in China.
Eopavo lived during the Miocene epoch.
The type species of the genus Eopavo is Eopavo hezhengensis.
facts.quote: Notes: A peafowl. The type species is E. hezhengensis.

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Eopavo is Eopavo hezhengensis.
Eopavo hezhengensis is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species Eopavo hezhengensis, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype of Eopavo hezhengensis is an incomplete skeleton including limb elements, synsacrum, pelvis, pectoral girdle, and vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Eopavo hezhengensis consists of an incomplete skeleton represented by elements of limb, synsacrum, pelvis, pectoral girdle, and vertebrae.

facts.statement: The holotype has a relatively long spur compared to its body size, suggesting it was a male.
facts.quote: It has a relatively long spur relative to its body size, suggesting the holotype represents a male individual.

facts.statement: Eopavo is classified within the clade Pavonini, which includes the living genera Pavo and Afropavo.
facts.quote: Morphological and phylogenetic analyses place Eopavo as a member of the clade Pavonini, which contains the extant peafowl genera Pavo and Afropavo.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Eopavo's small body size was likely an adaptation to the high-elevation savanna habitat it inhabited.
facts.quote: The small body size of Eopavo was likely linked to the high elevation of the savanna habitat it inhabited, which differs from extant peafowls.

facts.statement: Yu et al. (2026) suggested that the peafowl clade likely originated on the Tibetan Plateau.
facts.quote: Yu et al. (2026) also suggested that peafowl likely originated from Tibetan Plateau.

facts.statement: The long spur of Eopavo hezhengensis suggests it may have engaged in aggressive physical contact between males, similar to some modern relatives.
Eopavo lived in a high-elevation Miocene savanna habitat, unlike the humid forests preferred by modern peafowl.
Eopavo lived during the Late Miocene.
Eopavo hezhengensis was found in late Miocene deposits in the Linxia Basin, China, near the edge of the Tibetan Plateau.
The disjunct distribution of modern peafowl in southern Asia and central Africa has led to debates about the clade's origin and evolution.

rejected.statement: Eopavo was described by Yu et al. in 2026.
Eopavo is an extinct genus of small peafowl known from the Late Miocene Liushu Formation of China.
rejected.quote: Eopavo (meaning "dawn Pavo") is an extinct genus of small peafowl known from the Late Miocene Liushu Formation of China.
